note: Adapted from Sjöstedt's 1899 original description (in German), original name Eutermes camerunensis n. sp., with only the alate paragraph and measurements; type locality Cameroon (3 May 1892, month 5, collected by Dr. Brauns, specimen in the Hamburg Museum). The original measurements use a comma as the decimal separator, transcribed here as 6.5 mm etc.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate dorsal surface dark brown, the abdominal segments horny brown with darker sides forming a distinct patch over segments 4—5 above; posterior margins of the meso- and metanota broad and flat, very slightly incurved, without short pointed processes; the first two mandibular teeth small and equal; wing veins mostly very indistinct, the venation very faint; antennae 15-segmented; legs pale white. It differs from the other African species of the genus mainly in the posterior margins of the meso- and metanota lacking pointed processes, the degenerate wing venation and the 15-segmented antennae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Alate: dorsal surface dark brown, abdominal segments horny brown, darker laterally, forming a distinct patch over segments 4—5 above; wings pale brownish grey; posterior margins of the meso- and metanota broad and flat, slightly incurved, without short pointed processes; the first two mandibular teeth small and equal; wing veins mostly very indistinct; antennae 15-segmented; legs pale white. Measurements: body length with wings 12 mm; wing expanse 22 mm; wing length 10 mm, width 3 mm; body (with head) length 6.5 mm.
